summary.text: The counterexample is \(n=8=2^3\), for which \(\Omega(8)=3\), while the Möbius sum reduces to \(8!(H_8-H_4)=25584>0\). Thus the proposed criterion predicts negativity at \(8\), contrary to the actual positive value.

full_proof.text:
Let
\[
H_n=\sum_{j=1}^n\frac1j
\]
be the \(n\)-th harmonic number. The defining divisor relation for A067857 is
\[
\sum_{k\mid n}\frac{a(k)}{k!}=H_n.
\]
If we put \(b(k)=a(k)/k!\), this says that \(H_n=\sum_{k\mid n}b(k)\). Möbius inversion therefore gives
\[
b(n)=\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(n/d)H_d,
\]
and hence, for every positive integer \(n\),
\[
a(n)=n!\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(n/d)H_d.
\]
Here \(\mu\) is the ordinary Möbius function.

We disprove the proposed equivalence by taking \(n=8\).

First consider the claimed condition on the number of prime factors. Since
\[
8=2^3,
\]
and \(2\) is prime, the total number of prime factors of \(8\), counted with multiplicity, is
\[
\Omega(8)=3.
\]
Thus \(\Omega(8)\) is odd and is at least \(3\). Consequently, the right-hand side of the conjectured equivalence is true at \(n=8\).

It remains to compute the sign of \(a(8)\). The positive divisors of \(8\) are
\[
1,2,4,8.
\]
Therefore the Möbius-transform formula specializes to
\[
\begin{aligned}
a(8)
&=8!\sum_{d\mid 8}\mu(8/d)H_d\\
&=8!\bigl(\mu(8)H_1+\mu(4)H_2+\mu(2)H_4+\mu(1)H_8\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
The relevant Möbius values follow directly from their definition. A number divisible by the square of a prime has Möbius value zero, so
\[
\mu(8)=\mu(2^3)=0,
\qquad
\mu(4)=\mu(2^2)=0.
\]
For a prime the Möbius value is \(-1\), and \(\mu(1)=1\), so
\[
\mu(2)=-1,
\qquad
\mu(1)=1.
\]
Substitution leaves only two terms:
\[
a(8)=8!\bigl(H_8-H_4\bigr).
\]
Now
\[
H_8-H_4=\frac15+\frac16+\frac17+\frac18.
\]
Using the common denominator \(840\), this is
\[
\frac{168+140+120+105}{840}=\frac{533}{840}.
\]
In particular this difference is positive. More explicitly, since \(8!=40320=48\cdot840\),
\[
a(8)=40320\cdot\frac{533}{840}=48\cdot533=25584>0.
\]
(Equivalently, one may separately compute \(H_4=25/12\) and \(H_8=761/280\), whose difference is \(533/840\).)

Thus at \(n=8\) we have
\[
\Omega(8)=3,
\]
which is odd and at least \(3\), but
\[
a(8)=25584>0,
\]
so in particular \(a(8)<0\) is false. Hence the implication
\[
\bigl(\Omega(n)\text{ is odd and }\Omega(n)\ge 3\bigr)\Longrightarrow a(n)<0
\]
already fails for \(n=8\). Therefore the proposed biconditional, and thus the conjecture, is false.
